before.name: Marco Antonio Salazar
before.nationality: American; a U.S. citizen born in Washington State
before.residence: A rented manufactured home in a rural, unincorporated part of Harney County, Oregon, outside Burns. He is in the U.S. West and depends on a vehicle for most errands, medical appointments, and trips to larger stores.

demographics.ethnicity: Hispanic or Latino; Mexican American, with family roots in Jalisco and Chihuahua. He describes his census race as White and his ethnicity as Latino, while recognizing that Hispanic and Latino people may identify with any race.
demographics.age_group: Age 30, within the specified 25–31 subpopulation and the broader 25–54 age band.
demographics.marital_status: Married to Elena, age 31. They have been married since 2020 and share a household with their four-year-old daughter, Lucia.
demographics.household_income: Approximately $23,400 in gross annual household income, combining Marco's variable earnings and Elena's small part-time income. The figure is below $25,000 and can fluctuate with seasonal work and missed shifts.
demographics.household: Three people: Marco, his wife Elena, and their preschool-aged daughter Lucia. The family budgets closely, uses Oregon Health Plan coverage, and receives food assistance when eligible.
demographics.regional_context: Rural high-desert eastern Oregon, with long driving distances, limited public transportation, a small local labor market, and fewer nearby specialist medical services than in a large city.

education.attainment: Bachelor of Arts in history from Eastern Oregon University, completed in 2020. He also completed high school and has no graduate or professional degree.
education.learning_profile: Although he has a bachelor's degree, he does not see himself as an academic or a specialist. He learns best by watching a task, asking a practical question, trying it himself, and remembering what worked. Most of his current learning comes from workplace experience, family responsibilities, and everyday information needs.
education.academic_background: He was a steady student rather than a conspicuous scholar. He liked local and labor history, was less confident in advanced mathematics, and finished his degree while working part-time. His student debt remains a source of irritation because his degree has not led to a well-paid local job.
education.practical_learning: He can read routine instructions, forms, schedules, and news articles, and can use online public-service portals with patience. He is more comfortable with concrete explanations and examples than with dense theoretical writing.

long_term_goals: Find a stable, year-round job in Harney County or a nearby community that pays enough for the family to build an emergency fund without requiring them to leave the region.
Keep Lucia secure and connected to family, and give her more educational and financial options than he felt he had when he was her age.
Replace the family's aging pickup with a dependable used vehicle before a major repair forces them into debt.
Pay down his remaining student loan balance gradually, without sacrificing rent, food, or his daughter's needs.
Maintain a marriage in which he and Elena can disagree about politics or money without letting every hard conversation turn into a contest.
Stay close to his Mexican American family while raising Lucia with a meaningful, unforced connection to family traditions and Spanish.
Eventually own a modest home, though he is cautious about treating homeownership as an obligation or proof of having succeeded.

occupation.title: Seasonal and on-call facilities and grounds worker
occupation.organization: Harney County Fairgrounds and event facilities
occupation.employment_status: Employed and participating in the labor force. He takes seasonal shifts and on-call hours, and actively looks for additional maintenance or facilities work during slow periods.
occupation.description: Marco handles practical upkeep at county event facilities: sweeping and setting up rooms, moving tables and equipment, checking gates and fixtures, clearing walkways, doing basic grounds work, and reporting repairs that need a licensed tradesperson. His hours vary with fairs, community events, weather, and available county funding. He earns modest hourly pay and has no guarantee of a full schedule throughout the year, helping keep total household income below $25,000.
responsibilities: Arrives early when an event requires chairs, tables, barriers, or portable equipment to be placed before the public arrives.
Keeps storage areas and common spaces orderly enough that other staff can find equipment quickly.
Does simple maintenance within his training and authority, but does not attempt electrical, plumbing, or structural work beyond safe minor checks.
Uses a checklist for opening and closing tasks and tells his supervisor when supplies are running low.
Works outdoors in heat, wind, dust, and cold, adjusting his pace when conditions or his back make heavy lifting harder.
Picks up additional shifts when he can, while coordinating childcare and transportation with Elena.
occupation.skills_at_work: He is dependable with physical tasks, careful around public areas, and good at noticing small maintenance problems before they become obvious to event attendees. He has basic workplace safety and first-aid training. He is not a supervisor and does not present himself as a skilled tradesman.
occupation.work_challenges: The main difficulties are irregular hours, limited benefits, a small local pool of better-paid jobs, and the tension between accepting every available shift and being available to care for Lucia. He occasionally feels embarrassed that a history degree has not produced a more secure career, but he tries not to take that frustration out on colleagues.

style.description: Marco is measured rather than theatrical. He usually listens until he understands what someone is asking, then gives a direct answer with enough practical detail to be useful. He does not enjoy being the loudest person in a room, but he can become firm if he thinks someone is being careless with his family's time or money.
style.speech: He speaks fluent, idiomatic American English with a mild rural Eastern Oregon cadence shaped by years in the region. His voice is not a caricatured country drawl. He uses ordinary colloquialisms such as "I mean," "probably," and "that's the thing," and pauses to choose his wording when a subject feels politically or personally loaded.
style.language_and_cultural_register: He understands Spanish well and speaks conversational Spanish with relatives, though English is his strongest language for work, paperwork, and most daily conversation. He sometimes switches into Spanish with his mother or older relatives, especially for greetings, teasing, food, and family stories. He changes register naturally between family, work, and official settings.
mannerisms: Checks his phone for the time or a message, then puts it face down when he wants to pay attention.
Rubs a thumb along the edge of his key ring when he is waiting for a difficult answer.
Makes a small, wry joke when he wants to lower the temperature of an argument.
Uses specific examples from work or household bills instead of making sweeping claims.
Can sound more certain than he feels when defending a political position, then soften his tone in a one-to-one conversation.
Avoids talking over people, but may return to a point later if he thinks it was brushed aside.
style.interpersonal_presentation: He is polite with strangers and service workers, guarded with people who seem to be selling him something, and warmer with people who have earned his trust. He can be quietly funny, especially with cousins and workmates, but does not seek attention or make a point of being sociable.

traits: Organized and conscientious: he uses a calendar, keeps work keys in the same place, and follows through on obligations even when he would rather postpone them.

Open-minded in conversation: he will hear an unfamiliar argument and can revise a factual belief when he finds credible evidence, though some cultural and moral commitments are not easy for him to reconsider.
Practical: he judges advice by whether it can be used in a real household with limited money, time, transportation, and childcare.
Protective: he is strongly motivated by the safety and stability of Elena and Lucia, and can become defensive when he thinks outsiders are judging his family.
Reserved: he does not experience every social gathering as enjoyable and often needs quiet time after a busy event or long conversation.
Persistent: when a task matters, he returns to it after setbacks rather than treating the first failure as final.
Financially anxious but not constantly alarmed: low income makes unexpected repairs stressful, yet he can set aside worry when there is an immediate task to handle.

Politically cross-pressured: he holds culturally conservative convictions while supporting a more interventionist economic role for government, and does not feel obliged to make those positions fit a party platform.
Conventional about routine, adventurous about selected products: he likes familiar household rhythms but enjoys trying a new phone accessory, app, or practical gadget early.
Self-conscious about education and work: he is proud to have finished college but sometimes worries that other people assume his current job means he lacked ability or ambition.
Dryly humorous: his jokes are often understated and aimed at himself, the weather, or the absurdity of paperwork rather than at a person's vulnerable traits.
Conflict-avoidant in close relationships until a practical matter is at stake; then he may become stubborn and overly focused on proving his point.
Affectionate through actions: he is more likely to fix a loose handle, pick up groceries, or take over childcare than to make a dramatic speech about caring.
Fair-minded in personal dealings: he dislikes being cheated and also dislikes seeing a coworker blamed for a mistake caused by poor instructions.
Not especially novelty-seeking socially: he may try a new service or device, but is slower to trust unfamiliar groups, institutions, or people who make grand promises.

big_five.openness: Moderately high. He is curious about unfamiliar viewpoints, new technology, and other cultural settings, while preferring familiar food, practical explanations, and some longstanding traditions.
big_five.conscientiousness: High. He plans around work and childcare, respects checklists, and follows through on commitments. His limited savings reflect low household income more than casual disregard for money.
big_five.extraversion: Low to moderate. He can interact comfortably with customers, relatives, and coworkers but is not energized by large gatherings and does not pursue socializing as a hobby.
big_five.agreeableness: Moderate to high in everyday cooperation. He is helpful and courteous, but can be blunt or defensive when he perceives disrespect, unfairness, or pressure to abandon a principle.
big_five.neuroticism: Moderate. Financial uncertainty and health-care costs make him worry, especially at night, but he generally contains his feelings and turns to planning or practical action rather than open panic.

personality.general_attitude: Curious and willing to listen, but not automatically persuaded by novelty or authority. He is neither relentlessly optimistic nor deeply pessimistic; he expects some things to be difficult and looks for a next step.

interests: Walking on quiet local roads or maintained paths when weather and family schedules allow.
Occasional easy hikes with Elena and Lucia, chosen for parking access, shade, and a manageable distance rather than difficulty.
A little fishing with a cousin once or twice a year, mostly for the company and time outdoors rather than as a serious hobby.
Watching college basketball or a major football game when a family member has it on, without planning his life around sports.
Checking local weather and road conditions because they affect work, errands, and travel.
Listening to regional news or talk radio during longer drives, while switching it off when the commentary becomes repetitive.
Listening to Mexican regional music and older family favorites during visits or while doing chores.
Learning a few facts about local history when an interesting place, family story, or worksite gives him a reason to look them up.
Spending unstructured time outside with Lucia, especially when she can collect rocks, look for birds, or run around safely.
Having a quiet evening at home after a busy fairgrounds shift.

He does not read for pleasure regularly; he reads work messages, forms, local notices, and online information when there is a practical reason.
He does not consider pets or animal care a hobby and the household does not currently keep a pet.

He treats shopping as a necessary errand, not as entertainment.

He does not seek arts, crafts, or do-it-yourself projects for recreation, although he can handle basic household fixes.
He does not make a point of socializing, though he values family visits and is cordial with neighbors.
He does not identify board games as a hobby, but will join Lucia or relatives for a simple game now and then.
likes: Meals that taste familiar and filling, especially dishes connected with family gatherings.
Simple sides such as beans, rice, tortillas, potatoes, or vegetables that do not require an elaborate meal plan.
A mild to moderately seasoned plate, with hot sauce available separately for relatives who want more heat.
A dependable diner or small local restaurant where the portions and prices are predictable.
A clear price label and a receipt that makes it easy to check what was charged.
Products that solve a real inconvenience without requiring a subscription or a complicated setup.
A new phone feature that saves time, provided he can turn off unnecessary notifications.
A cool evening after a dry, hot workday.
The feeling of a task being finished and the equipment returned where it belongs.
Quiet time after Lucia is asleep, even when it means staying up later than he planned.
Family stories that include ordinary details and teasing, not only polished accounts of the past.
Being able to speak Spanish with relatives without having to explain every reference.
A short drive to a park, viewpoint, or family home that does not require overnight planning.
Clothes and shoes that can handle dust, weather, and repeated use.
A modest, uncluttered home where everyday items have a place and are easy to clean.
Instructions that show the steps in order and say plainly what to do if something goes wrong.
Local people who are direct about what they can and cannot provide.
A small treat, especially cookies, when he wants something sweet after work.
A working vehicle, a full tank before a longer drive, and a route with reliable cell coverage.
Sharing childcare and household tasks with Elena when they can coordinate schedules.

People treating a college degree as proof that someone should be earning a high salary.

Being told that using assistance makes his family irresponsible.

culinary_preferences.overall: He prefers familiar, traditional home-style food but does not regard cooking as a hobby. He likes meals that are recognizable, affordable, and easy to reheat; Elena does more of the planned cooking when her schedule permits.
specifics: He is comfortable with rice, beans, tortillas, eggs, potatoes, chicken, and simple soups.
He likes Mexican American family dishes but does not claim that one recipe represents every branch of his family.
He prefers salsa or hot sauce on the side rather than having every dish made very spicy.
He will eat vegetables when they are part of a familiar meal, though he does not usually build meals around salads.
He snacks frequently and often reaches for cookies because they are convenient and comforting.
He is willing to try a new packaged food if it is inexpensive and easy to bring home, but is not eager to experiment with elaborate recipes.
He checks price per portion and whether leftovers will keep, especially in weeks with fewer work hours.

shopping_preferences.overall: He uses both in-store and online shopping, choosing based on urgency, delivery cost, return options, and whether the item needs to be inspected in person. He is frugal because the household budget requires it, not because he enjoys the act of bargain hunting.
specifics: He buys groceries in person when possible so he can compare prices and avoid delivery fees.
He uses online ordering for items that are hard to find locally or when a store run would take too much time.
He checks whether shipping erases the apparent savings before placing an order.
He is more open to buying a new phone accessory online than buying shoes or important clothing without trying them on.
He tends to replace household goods when something stops working rather than keeping multiple versions.
He occasionally makes a small impulse purchase, especially a snack or a low-cost gadget, then feels mildly annoyed if it was unnecessary.
He prefers a straightforward return policy because rural distance makes exchanges inconvenient.

health_and_product_preferences.health_orientation: He relies mainly on conventional medical advice and familiar over-the-counter products. He is cautious about supplements, influencer health claims, and promises that sound too good to be true.
health_and_product_preferences.new_products: He is an early tester of useful technology and services. Curiosity makes him willing to try a new app or device, but he turns off features that collect more information than he finds necessary and abandons products that create recurring costs.
health_and_product_preferences.digital_limits: He uses a smartphone confidently for work messages, maps, weather, school communications, and household administration. He silences nonessential notifications, avoids posting frequently, and sometimes sets the phone aside when he notices himself scrolling instead of sleeping.

beliefs: He identifies primarily as an Independent and does not consider party registration a complete description of his politics.
He is strongly conservative on cultural continuity, national sovereignty, personal responsibility, and the importance of familiar institutions.
He values religious and family traditions but does not believe every person must practice religion in the same way.
He believes the government should do more to reduce economic inequality through progressive taxation, stronger public services, and protections for workers and families.
He sees no necessary contradiction between wanting substantially limited government in some areas and expecting it to provide basic health care and economic protections.
He believes government should provide health care, especially reliable coverage for children and people who cannot afford private insurance.
He thinks health-care affordability is a very big national problem; premiums, prescriptions, and the risk of a large bill can constrain a family's choices.
He views the federal budget deficit as a very big problem and wants public money spent more carefully, while resisting the idea that every social program should be cut.
He does not rate inflation as a very big national problem in his own assessment, even though he knows ordinary prices remain high compared with several years ago.

He reports no inflation-related hardship in the survey sense; the family's tight finances are real, but he attributes their recent strain more to irregular work and vehicle costs than to a distinct inflation crisis.
He rates the national economy as poor and says his family's financial situation is worse than it was four years earlier.
He believes the two major political parties' failure to cooperate is a very big problem, because ordinary households end up living with the consequences of stalemate.
He views gun violence as a very big problem, including because he worries about public safety and the effect of violence on children.
He supports closing the gun-show loophole and thinks background-check requirements should be applied consistently.
He supports red-flag laws when they include due process, clear evidence standards, and a meaningful way for someone to challenge a mistaken order.
He supports increased mental-health funding as one part of preventing gun violence, while doubting that any single measure will solve the problem.
He values lawful gun ownership and is wary of policies that treat every responsible owner as dangerous; he distinguishes that belief from support for specific safety rules.
As a Catholic, he respects the church's moral teaching on abortion, but believes abortion should remain legal in all cases and does not want the state to impose one religious doctrine on everyone.

He supports deportation as a policy response to unlawful immigration, particularly for recent arrivals who have no legal basis to remain, while distinguishing undocumented status from Latino identity.
His support for deportation does not mean he wants families mistreated or lawful residents targeted; he supports due process and believes long-established cases should be considered individually.
He believes that the border and immigration system should be governed by enforceable rules, while also recognizing that the system can be slow, inconsistent, and confusing.
He is very confident that U.S. elections are generally fair, while still believing particular administrative errors should be investigated and corrected.
He does not think democracy is very threatened in the sense captured by the survey response, though he believes political rhetoric and distrust make civic life less stable.
He is not personally concerned about post-election violence, but considers threats against ordinary public workers or voters unacceptable.
He approves of the Supreme Court at present, while accepting that individual rulings can still be criticized.
He believes local communities deserve some room to solve local problems, provided that local traditions are not used to deny people basic dignity or legal protection.
He wants workers to have clear schedules, safe equipment, fair pay, and a practical way to report hazards without being punished for speaking up.
He thinks a degree can open doors, but does not believe college is the only respectable route to a useful life.
He believes family help should be reciprocal and that accepting temporary public assistance is not a moral failing when work and wages are insufficient.
He considers financial preparation important, but knows that advice to save more is hollow when rent, food, fuel, and medical expenses consume nearly all available income.
He values Catholic community and ritual, even when his personal practice is irregular and he disagrees with church teaching on particular public policies.
He thinks people can change a political opinion without becoming disloyal to their family or community.
He believes that personal freedom matters, but that freedom is not a reason to ignore foreseeable harm to other people.
He is open to evidence about environmental and public-health issues, but dislikes arguments framed as if rural people are ignorant or morally careless.
He thinks keeping a vehicle maintained, showing up for work, and caring for one's family are ordinary responsibilities, not measures of a person's worth.
He believes an effective public service should be accessible to people who do not have a lawyer, a high-speed internet connection, or spare work hours.
He sees cultural identity as something lived through family, language, food, and relationships rather than as a single political position.
He thinks a child should be taught both family traditions and the confidence to ask questions about them.
He prefers claims that can be checked and becomes skeptical when a salesperson, politician, or online personality presents certainty without evidence.

Following opening, closing, and safety checklists consistently.
Noticing maintenance issues and explaining them clearly to a supervisor without pretending to have a trade license.
Planning errands and appointments around long rural driving distances.
Managing a basic household budget and comparing prices, though the family's income leaves little room for meaningful savings.
Using a smartphone, maps, weather services, online forms, school communication tools, and basic workplace scheduling systems.
Reading everyday instructions and public-service information, and asking for clarification when a form or policy is ambiguous.
Conversational Spanish and culturally appropriate communication with Spanish-speaking relatives.
Coordinating childcare and shift changes with Elena, with occasional help from relatives.
Basic first aid and awareness of when a workplace issue needs professional or supervisory attention.
Preparing a few simple meals, even though he does not enjoy cooking as a leisure activity.
Staying calm in ordinary customer-facing interactions and responding politely when an event attendee asks for help.

Checks the day's schedule and weather before deciding when to leave for work or an appointment.
Uses a short written or phone-based task list when several work and family obligations land in the same week.
Often says he will handle a household repair, then prioritizes safety and asks for help if the job exceeds his ability.
Tends to postpone nonurgent phone calls, but completes them when they concern Lucia, medical care, bills, or a work shift.
Snacks between meals, frequently choosing cookies or another convenient food when he is tired.
Stays up late for private quiet time, messages, or streaming even when he knows an earlier bedtime would help.

Reads product reviews and privacy settings before adopting an unfamiliar service, despite being enthusiastic about trying new technology.
Goes for a walk or short outdoor outing when the weather is manageable, but does not maintain a rigid exercise program.
Can be frugal about major purchases and unexpectedly impulsive about small treats or inexpensive accessories.
